findings: The global physics_checks list has no per-control or phase applicability, yet it combines mutually incompatible requirements. For example, untouched-initial-zero-score requires zero fractures and fragments, while the same list requires four fractures, four contained fragments, terminal hold, and completed strikes. It also simultaneously requires qualified off-axis impulse <=0.008 N*s and invalid-strike off-axis impulse >0.008 N*s. Define an explicit check-to-control/phase matrix or separate initialization, success, and adversarial-control checks. input/last-failure.json demonstrates the practical ambiguity: an environment attempt failed the globally stated completed-insert-strike-count-minimum even though that check cannot apply to untouched, slow-press, or other zero-strike controls.

completed-insert-strike-count-minimum is internally contradictory. Its scalar threshold is >=1, but damage_rules says each of all four inserts must have at least one closed strike causing its credited transition. Specify either a completed-insert count with threshold >=4 or four per-insert Boolean/count observables, including aggregation and applicability. The current name, threshold, and prose cannot all be true.

Several extrema are undefined for controls with empty qualifying sets, including credited-impact-axis-angle-maximum, credited-impact-radial-offset-maximum, and qualified-strike impulse extrema. The contract correctly says callback/contact-stream failure cannot silently become zero, but it does not define whether genuinely empty eligible sets are not-applicable, unavailable, or assigned a sentinel. Explicit empty-set and availability rules are required per control to prevent numerical vacuous passes like those described in input/request.json.

The 17 scores otherwise recompute correctly in stated order as 0.00, 0.20, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.30, 0.85, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 0.00, 1.00, 1.00, 1.00, 0.20, 0.20. R first becomes available only after the fourth credited fracture; full score is 0.10+0.10+0.40+0.10+0.20+0.10=1.00. Timeout changes the inaccessible-fragment control by evaluating geometric inaccessibility first and setting H, producing zero.

Timing is consistent: 7,200 controls at 20 Hz is 360 s; production/refinement use 240/480 Hz; 300 s corresponds to POST 72,000/144,000 and timeout to POST 86,400/172,800. PRE/POST freshness, force-versus-impulse conversion, float32 dt-error maxima <=1e-9 s, reset clearing, callback-exception invalidation, portable-case handling, case-relative insert transforms, and initial shell/seat integrity are explicitly specified.

Primary evidence supports four M2.5 x 3.75 mm inserts, tang removal, ensuring tangs do not remain, notch fracture, portable shell reorientation, the 61 g completed shell assembly, and M2.5 tang-break mandrel 0158 040 1000. Unpublished forces, tolerances, geometry, and masses remain disclosed as prototype assumptions. The pinned PhysxManager snapshot hash matches its index and confirms dt-bearing PRE_PHYSICS_STEP/POST_PHYSICS_STEP subscriptions and removable callback handles; this establishes API availability only, as the contract correctly states.
